## What's new in v2.0.51

### Network Map: IP addresses on access points
On a router working as an access point behind a main router, devices showed *IP from main router* instead of their address. An access point never hands out addresses, so it only knew the IPs of devices it had talked to.

While the map is open, the router now pings each address of its LAN in the background once every 5 minutes, at most 16 at a time. Devices answer the router's address lookup even if they ignore ping, so their IPs show up within about 20 seconds. Normal routers are unaffected: they already know every IP from DHCP. You can switch it off under *System → UniWRT Theme → Network Map → Find device IP addresses on access points*.

### Network Map: activity dot next to the name
The green/grey activity dot now sits right after each device name (for example *Kitchen-CCTV ●*) instead of crowding the top corner of the card. It is now steady instead of pulsing (see below).

### New: "Upgrade all" on the Software page
On OpenWrt 25.12+ (apk), *System → Software → Updates* now has an **Upgrade all (N)…** button, next to *Update lists…*. It shows how many packages have updates, asks for confirmation, then runs the page's own `apk upgrade` and shows the output. Nothing new runs as root: it is the same command and permission LuCI already uses to upgrade one package. It isn't offered with opkg (OpenWrt 23.05 / 24.10), where OpenWrt warns that upgrading every package can break a router.

### Smoother, lighter Network Map
Measured in the browser, the map now does about a quarter less work per second:
- The pulsing activity dots cost as much as all the animated traffic lines together, so the dot is now steady (with a soft glow when active).
- The traffic lines pause automatically while the map is scrolled out of view.
It still runs at a steady 60 fps, with the same single request to the router per refresh.

### Upgrading
Run the install line below again (standalone), or install the new package, then reload the page.
